name: Waygate Technologies inspection portfolio, now part of Hexagon
summary: Hexagon closed its acquisition of Waygate Technologies from Baker Hughes on November 2, Waygate announced. The deal was first announced on April 13. Waygate makes non-destructive testing equipment, including industrial computed tomography, field radiography, ultrasonic testing and remote visual inspection, the category that includes the videoscopes and borescopes used in engine shops, and it describes its tools as increasingly cloud-based and AI-enhanced. It now sits in Hexagon's Manufacturing Intelligence business, which is known for coordinate measuring machines, portable measuring devices, scanners and metrology software. The companies say combining them covers a part from its outside dimensions and surface through to its internal structure, for customers in aerospace, automotive and other industries. Waygate says customers keep their familiar products, services and contacts, and that ongoing projects, service agreements and orders continue without interruption. No product changes were announced.

whyItMatters: Inspection equipment is only as useful as the service and software support behind it, and a borescope that is down for calibration is an engine that cannot be signed off. If your shop runs Waygate equipment, nothing changes today, but this is a good moment to confirm your service agreement, software updates and any AI defect-detection features you rely on are carried forward. Shops buying new inspection kit can ask whether surface scanning and internal inspection data will land in one record, which cuts the time spent matching findings by hand.
